title: Senator Lisa Murkowski highlights new laws addressing fentanyl dangers and support for FASD
text:

U.S. Senator Lisa Murkowski | Lisa Murkowski Official website
Senator Lisa Murkowski has highlighted recent legislative efforts on social media, focusing on substance use disorders and support for those affected by Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD). Her posts detail the passage of Bruce’s Law and ongoing advocacy related to FASD.
On December 1, 2025, Murkowski referenced the story of Sandy Snodgrass, a mother who lost her son to fentanyl poisoning. She wrote: "Four years ago, Sandy Snodgrass faced every parent’s worst nightmare when she lost her son to fentanyl poisoning, but she turned her heartache into advocacy for families and those who struggle with substance use across the country. Now that Bruce’s Law has been signed into law,".
In another post dated December 2, 2025, Murkowski discussed services for individuals affected by FASD. She stated: "Those affected by FASD need access to services across the board, including early intervention, medical resources, and tailored educational and behavioral support. It’s why Senator Klobuchar and I have been so persistent regarding the Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders Respect Act".
Continuing this theme on December 3, 2025, Murkowski revisited the loss experienced by Sandy Snodgrass in 2021 and noted legislative progress. She posted: "In 2021, Sandy Snodgrass lost her son, Bruce, to fentanyl poisoning. Yesterday, after years of her advocacy, legislation that carries Bruce’s name was signed into law raising awareness on substance use disorders and the dangers of fentanyl in communities across America. I was https://t.co/j6fiN0j5VG".
Bruce’s Law aims to increase public understanding about substance use disorders and highlight risks associated with fentanyl exposure. The legislation is named after Bruce Snodgrass following advocacy efforts led by his mother after his death in 2021.
Murkowski also referenced collaborative work with Senator Amy Klobuchar on advancing federal support for individuals living with FASD through targeted acts like the Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders Respect Act.
